title: Anatomy of an HTTP Request
learning_objectives: Name the parts of an HTTP/1.1 request: request line, headers, blank line, body
Parse a raw request into method, target, version, headers and body
Treat header names case-insensitively and use Content-Length
Classify methods as safe and idempotent
entry_point: parse_request(raw); build_request(method, target, headers=None, body=''); is_safe(method); is_idempotent(method)
hints: Check `"\r\n\r\n" in raw` first; `lines[0].split(" ")` must give 3 parts; `method.isalpha() and method.isupper()`.
For each header line use `name, sep, value = line.partition(":")`; if `sep` is empty raise ValueError.
Body length in bytes: `len(body.encode("utf-8"))`. Idempotent methods are the safe ones plus PUT and DELETE.

failure_feedback.advice: Lowercase header names and strip their values.
Split each header at the first colon only (`str.partition`).
Check the blank line, the three-part request line, the method, the version, header colons and Content-Length.
Join lines with CRLF, end headers with a blank line, and add Content-Length in bytes for non-empty bodies.
Idempotent = GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE; compare in upper case.
